back2basics.text: The Census of India collects demographic data including caste to aid policy formulation and social justice measures. Caste enumeration is typically done in phases, with Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes having predefined lists, while Other Backward Classes (OBCs) are recognised under constitutional provisions. Accurate caste data helps in targeted welfare schemes and affirmative action. The use of digital tools and data entry methods affects the reliability of this data.

2026-10-29-am-06cb0ce035.deck: The Supreme Court permitted the OBC Federation of India to approach the Registrar General for including a pre-loaded drop-down menu of OBC castes in Census 2027 digital tools. This development highlights constitutional and policy debates on caste enumeration methods relevant for social justice and governance.

back2basics.concept: Role of Parliament in International Diplomacy
back2basics.text: Parliaments play a crucial role in shaping a country's foreign policy through legislation, oversight, and representation. Parliamentary diplomacy involves dialogue and cooperation between legislatures of different countries to build mutual understanding, support peaceful dispute resolution, and promote shared development goals. This complements executive diplomacy and strengthens democratic accountability in international relations.

The forum issued a joint declaration supporting a two-state solution for the Israel-Palestine conflict and condemned unilateral sanctions and terrorism.

back2basics.text: Dearness Allowance (DA) is a cost of living adjustment allowance paid to government employees to offset inflation. Dearness Relief (DR) is the equivalent allowance paid to pensioners. Both are calculated as a percentage of basic pay or pension and are revised periodically based on inflation indices to protect the purchasing power of employees and pensioners.

2026-10-29-am-1384231961.deck: The Union Cabinet approved a 3% increase in Dearness Allowance (DA) and Dearness Relief (DR) for central government employees and pensioners effective from July 1, 2026. This decision impacts over 1.17 crore beneficiaries and has a fiscal implication of ₹10,016.10 crore annually, reflecting government welfare and fiscal policy management.

back2basics.text: The CBD is an international treaty aimed at conserving biodiversity, promoting sustainable use of its components, and ensuring fair sharing of benefits arising from genetic resources. Parties to the CBD meet regularly at Conferences of the Parties (COP) to negotiate and implement biodiversity goals globally. India, as a party, aligns its policies and actions with the CBD framework to protect its rich biodiversity.

2026-10-29-am-56388efe33.deck: At the 17th Conference of the Parties (COP-17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) in Yerevan, India released four important publications on biodiversity conservation, biosafety, and access and benefit sharing. This highlights India's role in global biodiversity governance and its efforts to implement international commitments through policy, finance, and innovation.

back2basics.concept: Child Protection Laws and Digital Crime
back2basics.text: Child protection laws aim to safeguard children from exploitation, abuse, and trafficking, including digital forms such as child pornography. Digital crime laws regulate the use of technology and internet platforms to prevent and penalize offenses like non-consensual sharing of explicit content. Intermediaries such as online platforms have responsibilities under law to remove illegal content and report it to authorities.

2026-10-29-am-5cc90d51f5.deck: The Union government told the Supreme Court on October 27, 2026, that it is contemplating a statutory legislative framework to address child pornography and non-consensual explicit content involving adults. This development is important for understanding the evolving legal measures on child protection and digital crime enforcement.

back2basics.text: The IIP measures the short-term changes in the volume of production of a basket of industrial products during a given period compared to a base period. It is a key economic indicator used to assess industrial sector performance and overall economic health. The base year is the reference year against which changes in production are measured, and updating it ensures the index reflects current industrial realities.

2026-10-29-am-64b82ecee0.deck: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) held a three-day workshop from 28 to 30 October 2026 in Thiruvananthapuram to revise the base year of the State-level Index of Industrial Production (IIP) to 2022-23. This revision updates the industrial performance measurement framework, which is crucial for economic analysis and policy formulation.

back2basics.text: A Maritime Board is a statutory body responsible for managing port and maritime activities within a state. State legislatures can amend laws governing such boards to improve governance, operational efficiency, and development. These amendments may affect coastal communities, environmental regulations, and economic infrastructure, highlighting the balance between development and rights protection.

They function under the Panchayati Raj system, which decentralizes governance to empower local communities. Effective rural governance requires integration of planning, resource management, and community participation to address local needs and implement government schemes.

body.text: It brings together planning processes of Central Ministries and State Governments on a common digital platform to prepare Gram Panchayat Development Plans (GPDPs) that identify gaps, align interventions, and optimize resource use.

body.label: Digital governance
body.text: Building on eGramSwaraj and e-Panchayat systems, the scheme consolidates information on government schemes, beneficiaries, community assets, and resources on a single digital platform to improve planning, coordination, and monitoring.

body.label: Capacity building and awareness
body.text: The scheme supports capacity building for around 32 lakh governance stakeholders annually and uses digital and outreach platforms, including PANCHAM, to reach at least 1 crore citizens per awareness episode, fostering informed community discussions.

body.label: Financial accountability
body.text: It strengthens Panchayats’ ability to utilize Finance Commission grants and other funds effectively, mobilize Own Source Revenue, and ensures online accounting, auditing, and public disclosure to promote transparency and financial self-reliance.

sections.heading: How does the scheme strengthen rural governance?

body.label: Implementation framework
body.text: The scheme will be implemented through State Governments and Union Territory Administrations, which will submit Annual Action Plans for appraisal and approval by a designated Central Empowered Committee.

body.label: Use of existing systems
body.text: It leverages existing institutional, capacity-building, digital, and communication systems at the grassroots level without creating permanent posts but may engage contractual personnel as needed for technical support.

body.label: Alignment with Finance Commission
body.text: The scheme period aligns with the Sixteenth Finance Commission's period, which recommends around ₹4.35 lakh crore in grants for Rural Local Bodies, enabling Panchayats to use these resources more effectively.

back2basics.concept: State Election Commission and Electoral Roll Revision
back2basics.text: State Election Commissions are constitutional bodies responsible for conducting elections to local bodies like municipalities and panchayats. They operate independently of the Election Commission of India, which conducts elections for Parliament and state legislatures. Electoral roll revision is the process of updating the list of eligible voters to ensure accuracy and prevent fraud, often done through special intensive revisions or periodic updates.

Ashok, Leader of Opposition in Karnataka Assembly, accused the State Election Commission (SEC) of printing 90 lakh voter identity cards after the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) announcement, alleging irregularities in upcoming local polls. The SEC denied the charge, stating the printing tender was floated before the SIR and within legal bounds.

mcq.stem:
Consider the following statements regarding the recent controversy over voter card printing in Bengaluru:
1. The State Election Commission printed 90 lakh voter identity cards after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) announcement.
2. The tender for printing voter cards was floated before the SIR announcement under rules applicable to local body elections.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
mcq.trap: Statement 1 is incorrect because the SEC denied printing cards after the SIR announcement, stating the tender was floated before SIR.

body.label: Printing after SIR
body.text: R. Ashok alleged that the SEC printed 90 lakh voter identity cards in Bengaluru after the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) announcement, violating norms.

body.label: Excess cards
body.text: He pointed out that Bengaluru's total voters after SIR were about 59 lakh, so the extra 31 lakh cards are 'bogus' and could be used for vote theft.

body.label: Demand for probe
body.text: Ashok accused the Congress government of involvement and demanded a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the matter.

body.label: Supreme Court affidavit
body.text: He cited that the SEC had filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court stating local body elections would be held only after SIR and preparation of a new voters’ list.

sections.heading: What are the allegations made by R. Ashok against the State Election Commission?

body.label: Tender timing
body.text: The SEC Secretary, Amaresh H., denied the allegations, stating the tender for printing voter cards was floated before the SIR announcement.

body.label: Legal mandate
body.text: The SEC acted under Rule 26 of the Greater Bengaluru Governance (Registration of Electors) Rules, 2025, which permits printing voter identity cards.

body.label: SIR non-binding
body.text: The SEC clarified that the SIR by the Election Commission of India is not binding on it, as local body elections and ECI elections follow different frameworks.

body.label: Purpose of printing
body.text: The printing aimed to prevent impersonation, especially in densely populated urban areas.

sections.heading: How did the State Election Commission respond to the allegations?

body.label: Electoral process understanding
body.text: It highlights the distinction between the Election Commission of India and State Election Commissions in managing electoral rolls and conducting elections.

body.label: Constitutional bodies' autonomy
body.text: The case exemplifies issues related to the autonomy and legal mandates of constitutional and statutory electoral bodies.

body.label: Election integrity concerns
body.text: It raises questions on electoral roll revisions, voter identity management, and potential misuse impacting election fairness.
